sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Woerden, a small city in the province of Utrecht, charges for parking in the centre and is deciding whether to extend regulation south of the station, where new homes are coming. The council adopted the parking tax ordinance for 2026 on 27 November 2025. The paid zones 4400, 4401 and 4404 cost 0.32 euro per 6 minutes, or 3.20 euros an hour, with maximum stays of 180, 30 and 120 minutes, while zone 4403 costs 6.20 euros an hour up to 24.80 euros a day [0]. Paid parking applies Monday to Saturday from 10:00 to 18:30, and in zone 4403 until 22:00, under a decision of 9 December 2025 [1]. A first resident permit costs 240.20 euros and a second 480.40 euros, though the published table does not state the period; visitor parking costs 0.32 euro an hour with a ceiling of 96 euros per calendar year, and the penalty charge is 82 euros [2]. Permits are capped, with 790 permits for 844 permit-zone spaces and at most 57 second permits, and the commuter permit is valid only on Oostsingel and Oostlaan [3]. The municipality's parking vision is fewer cars on the street, especially in the centre, garages preferred and residential parking mainly for residents [13]. For the area south of the station, a consultation in February and March 2025 drew 475 ideas and comments, 248 of them for Stationsgebied and Hoofdstedenbuurt, and the most frequent opinion was to keep parking free. The council was expected to decide in early October 2025, and we found no decision [10]. The municipality says high parking pressure at the P&R Houttuinlaan, with parkers using neighbouring streets, is a reason for extra rules, and that it wants to regulate the P&R Zuid site while investigating whether parking for travellers can stay free [8][11].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: Housing drives the changes. The municipality expects homes close to the bus and train station over the next 15 years, with Snellerpoort having fewer public parking spaces, and says new-build residents must park on their own land under lower parking norms, with no plans for extra public parking [8][11]. In Nieuw-Middelland it lists 134 homes at Watermolenlaan 1 and 132 at Watermolenlaan 4/Houttuinlaan 5, both expected to start in 2026 with half-sunken parking cellars, 59 homes at Zaagmolenhof 4 and 285 rental homes at Houttuinlaan 6-12 from the end of 2027 [15][16]. Works for a sewer bypass in the Houttuinlaan start on 19 October 2026, with the street closed for four weeks [16]. The Omgevingsvisie of 2022, published on the digital permit counter in January 2026, aims at a car-light centre, wider regulated parking and lower parking norms for new development, and planned to build the Rembrandtbrug in 2026 [14]. The municipality plans to place charge points based on data at the end of the year, so residents no longer need to apply for them [17].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The Castellum garage, at Meulmansweg 8, charges 2.50 euros an hour from Monday to Saturday 08:00 to 18:30, is free in the evening, at night and on Sundays, and has a day ticket of 18.60 euros [4]. Subscriptions from 1 April 2026 cost 777 euros a year for a full one, 518 euros for off-peak and 206 euros for residents, with a ceiling of 220 residents' subscriptions [5]. The terms for the Defensie-eiland garage carry the same tariff but still name the Castellum address, so they appear copied, and we cannot say what is charged there [6]. Q-Park lists a single site in Woerden, P+R Spoorlaan, with 172 spaces, open round the clock; its tariff did not load, and no source ties it to the 'P&R Noord' or 'P&R Zuid' names the municipality uses [7].

Our data cover the P+R Spoorlaan, with 172 spaces, for about 61 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 36% on weekdays and 23% at weekends, with a single reading at full on a Tuesday afternoon. The garages and street parking are not in our data.
